issues.legal_issue: A composite lease of a building and business equipment falls outside rent-control protection when its dominant purpose is the transfer of a business rather than the letting of the building as such.
material_facts: The lease covered a cinema building together with projectors, furniture, fittings, and other equipment needed to operate a cinema.
The parties treated the separate lease documents as a single transaction, and the tenant admitted that running a cinema business was an industrial purpose.
The rent attributed to the cinema equipment substantially exceeded the rent attributed to the building itself.
The building had already operated as a cinema, and the lease was to commence with the first film show.
The court found that the equipment and cinema business were the primary subject of the transaction and that the building was secondary, though necessary.
issues.conclusion: The lease was not an accommodation within the Act, and the landlord was entitled to a decree of eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(a) of the U.P. (Temporary) Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1947, accommodation concerns a building or part of a building and ancillary items that improve its beneficial enjoyment. For a composite lease with multiple purposes, the dominant purpose of the demise determines its character. A lease primarily transferring a business or industrial undertaking, with the building incidental to that transfer, is not a lease of accommodation. The Court applied the dominant-intention reasoning in Uttam Chand v. S. M. Lalwani.

rule.if: rent_control_scope_dispute and composite_lease and business_is_primary_subject and building_is_incidental and equipment_serves_business

predicates.rent_control_scope_dispute: The dispute concerns whether premises let under a composite transaction receive rent-control protection.
predicates.composite_lease: The lessor transferred a building together with equipment or other assets in a combined transaction.
predicates.business_is_primary_subject: The parties' transaction primarily transferred a business or undertaking rather than the building as such.
predicates.building_is_incidental: The building served as the location for the transferred business and was secondary to the main subject of the transaction.
predicates.equipment_serves_business: The equipment transferred was primarily intended to operate the business rather than to make occupation of the building more convenient.

issues.definition: When a rent-control dispute concerns a composite lease in which the business and its operating equipment are primary and the building is incidental, the rule yields an eviction decree.

issues.legal_issue: A proviso excluding certain business premises does not expand a clear principal definition of protected accommodation to include business leases.
material_facts: The principal definition described accommodation by reference to a building or part of a building and specified ancillary items.
An amendment added a proviso excluding accommodation used as a factory or for an industrial purpose when the business was also leased in the same transaction.
The court considered the definition clear as to its building-focused scope and treated the proviso as clarifying an exclusion that might otherwise be mistaken for a building tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The proviso did not enlarge the protected category to include leases whose dominant subject was a business.
issues.legal_principle: A proviso is ordinarily read in relation to the principal enacting provision and is not a separate or independent enactment. The whole section should be read harmoniously, but where the principal provision is clear, a proviso cannot expand or limit it; it may clarify possible doubts. The Court cited Commissioner of Income-tax v. Indo-Mercantile Bank Ltd., M/s. Ram Narain Sons Ltd. v. Asst. Commissioner of Sales Tax, Thompson v. Dibdin, Rex v. Dibdin, and Tahsildar Singh v. State of U.P. on the construction of provisos.

predicates.statutory_proviso_interpretation_dispute: The dispute requires the court to interpret a proviso alongside a principal statutory definition.
predicates.principal_definition_is_clear: The court reads the principal definition as having a clear scope without relying on the proviso to create that scope.
predicates.proviso_identifies_a_possible_exclusion: The proviso expressly addresses a category that could otherwise be mistaken for falling within the principal definition.

issues.definition: When a proviso addresses a possible exclusion from a clear principal definition, the rule means that the proviso does not expand that definition.
